app.notes: Rapid 2.5.7 (Meta's AI-assisted OpenStreetMap editor), production bundle (dist/rapid.min.js) built with the repo's own `npm run all` on node 22.12.0 (pinned in mise.toml). .ui-capture/build-site.sh assembles .ui-capture/site (dist + local copies of CDN assets + an index.html adjusted only for offline/local API use). .ui-capture/start.sh runs .ui-capture/stub-server.mjs, which serves the site and all stubs on $PORT (4487). Data: .ui-capture/gen-world.mjs builds data/world.json from the real OSM extract of Three Rivers, Michigan that ships with Rapid (data/intro_graph.json: ~5,900 nodes/ways/relations - ~350 buildings, streets, river, parks, ~40 named shops/amenities), given realistic OSM ids, versions, timestamps, editors and changesets spread 2009-2026, plus light enrichment (addresses, opening hours, phones, building levels). Signed-in user riverbend_maya (account since 2019, 1,287 changesets, 3 unread messages) with 90 commented changesets over 2019-2026 (70 in the last 9 months) shown in the save panel's recent comments; ~1/3 of features were last edited by them (History panel). 22 OSM notes (open and closed, with discussion threads). 15 other mappers. Esri datasets 'St. Joseph County, MI Address Points' (158 suggested address points on unaddressed buildings) and 'City of Three Rivers Sidewalks' (34 sidewalk lines) are enabled as Rapid AI/open-data suggestions. Browser state (seed-prefs.js, applied once to localStorage) makes it a returning user: welcome/what's-new already seen, walkthrough completed, recent presets, hashtag #MapThreeRivers, last changeset comment, Custom imagery as last-used background. If opened without a map hash it jumps to the user's home area in downtown Three Rivers at z17. Main areas: map canvas with OSM data and imagery; top bar (Point/Line/Area/Note, Rapid AI features toggle, undo/redo, Save, account menu with avatar); right-hand map controls and panes (Background, Map Data incl. notes layer and Rapid datasets, Issues, Preferences, Help, keyboard shortcuts); selecting a feature opens the left inspector (preset, fields, tags, history). Rebuild everything: `.ui-capture/build-site.sh && node .ui-capture/gen-world.mjs`. Not verified in a real browser from inside the build sandbox (Chromium cannot launch under the macOS sandbox); all served URLs were checked with HTTP requests.

prompt:
This is a checkout of meta/Rapid (https://github.com/meta/Rapid) at commit 249abff91e69. The OpenStreetMap editor driven by open data, AI, and supercharged features

I want to see its user interface in a desktop browser, in the state a real, established user would see it. Please get the app running locally with its main interface working and realistic data in it.

# Running it
- Follow the repo's own setup docs and tooling. Take the simplest route that shows the real app: a static production build if the front end works without a backend, otherwise the app's own server (production or dev mode).
- If it needs a database or other services, run them locally with an embedded or file-based option (SQLite, in-memory, JSON files, an embedded Postgres such as PGlite) or the app's demo/mock mode.
- Don't redesign or restyle anything. Change only what's needed to build and run it.

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):
- Give the required variables placeholder values so the app starts.
- Where it actually calls the service, make the call succeed locally with realistic responses: use the app's own mock, test or offline mode if it has one; otherwise point the client at a small local stub server that start.sh also starts, or swap in a stub at the integration boundary (the API client or service module). Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.
- Calls the browser makes directly to outside services count too; point them at the local stub.
- For sign-in through an outside provider, create a local account or use the app's dev sign-in so you can get past it.
List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. No lorem ipsum or "Test 1".

# Environment
This shell is sandboxed: you can write only inside this directory (package-manager caches already point into ./.ui-capture/cache), and the network reaches only package registries, mise's download sources and GitHub (registry.npmjs.org, registry.yarnpkg.com, repo.yarnpkg.com, github.com, codeload.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, nodejs.org, mise.jdx.dev, mise-versions.jdx.dev, release-assets.githubusercontent.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, binaries.prisma.sh, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com). Docker isn't available. A process you start in the background can't be seen or stopped from a later command, so test servers on another port than 4487 (e.g. 5487) or in the foreground under `timeout`; anything still listening on 4487 is stopped before I check.

# When you're done, leave this in ./.ui-capture/
- app.json: {"mode": "static" or "server", "entry": "/path where the main UI opens", "login": null or {"username": "...", "email": "...", "password": "..."}, "stubs": [{"service": "what was faked", "how": "how"}], "notes": "how you set it up, what data is loaded, and the main areas of the app"}
- static mode: the production build in ./.ui-capture/out, with index.html as its entry. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server; unknown paths fall back to index.html.
- server mode: ./.ui-capture/start.sh, which starts everything the app needs (stubs included) in the foreground and serves the UI at http://localhost:4487/ (it gets PORT=4487). It runs with the same PATH and restrictions as your shell, plus no network at all except localhost, so everything must already be installed, built and seeded (or seeded by start.sh itself).
- Put any scripts you write for seeding or stubbing in ./.ui-capture/ too; they're kept with the setup record.

# Order of work
You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
1. Get the app building and running with its stubs, and write the contract above (app.json plus out/ or start.sh), even if it has only a little data so far.
2. Then build out the data, re-running your seed and checking the app still loads after each substantial step, so that a working state with the data loaded so far is always in place.
Write large data sets with a short generator script rather than as one long literal file.
